scope: The standing museum cut into the Derwent peninsula, including its concrete and rust-colored south face, terraced roof and Courtyard House entrance, ferry stair approach, and the adjoining Pharos and Round House envelopes.

originalReview.notes: Barrylb’s exact 2011 riverfront view shows the standing long rust-colored wedge panels, broad concrete grille sections and stepped entrance pavilions behind them.
Gary Houston’s exact 2017 wide river view shows the eastern end, low steel fronts, riverbank and above-grade museum additions. Construction cranes and temporary objects are outside scope.
Gary Houston’s exact view along the ferry landing documents the narrow long stair, sparse rails, cut and lower landing hut.

quallaSearch.notes: Exact Qualla exterior photographs support the original riverfront face and eastern stairs. Tasmania’s published native two-metre digital elevation crop records the actual peninsula relief. Works of art, indoor exhibits, hotel lodges and the detached estate pavilions are outside scope.

excludedHistoricalImagery.reason: Attribution-conditioned or redundant photography, and interior or art subjects outside the exterior scope.
